trans-unit.target: Social network icons, each linking to the URL of your choice
Inserts the dashboard's social links, without redefining them
Link the site to your Bluesky account, with no app to create and no password to type. Done once, then again if the access is withdrawn.
See every post at its date and time, and move it with a drag.
The agency's own part: the access at Google, the two keys, and the consent. Done once, then again the day the token is revoked.
Moderate what Google brought in, answer it, and put the reviews on a page.
The agency's part: the LinkedIn app, its two keys, and the consent. Done once, then every 60 days, the length of the access.
One single list for the whole site, rendered wherever the social links block is put
The agency's part: the Meta app, its two keys, and the consent. Done once, then again if the access is withdrawn.
Your posts for the networks: generate a series or prepare one, proofread its texts and medias, then approve or send it.
Several drafts at once, at a steady pace: choose the pace, where the texts and the media come from, then generate the drafts to proofread.
Pick the networks offered to your visitors, their order and their look
Click "Connect" on the "Bluesky" tile, then grant access on Bluesky. The site stores the session by itself.

Optional, in the configuration: search for "social-bluesky-handle" and put the account's handle in it, for instance example.bsky.social, for the next connection to offer it at once. Left empty, the account is picked on Bluesky's page.
Unfold "Subscribe from a calendar" and create the secret address: pasted into Outlook, Evolution or Google Calendar, it shows the planned posts there. Renewing it cuts the former one.
Drag a post onto a coming time of the week, or onto a coming day of the month where it keeps its time: it is planned there, its approval unchanged.
"New post" opens a post to write, planned at the next quarter of an hour. A double click on a coming time of the week, or on a day of the month, opens it at that very moment.
The week of posts: those gone out, and every coming one at its date and time, red to approve, green approved. "Month" shows the whole month. The hours shown are set in the configuration.
Click a post: its panel changes its date and time, approves it or takes it back to a draft, or opens its texts to edit them.
The "Connections" screen, in the sidebar's "Social" submenu: each network has its tile there, with its state and its "Connect" button.
Click "Connect" on the "Google Business Profile" tile, then grant access with the Google account owning the listing. The site stores the token, the account and the listing by itself.

Search for "social-google-oauth-client-id" and "social-google-oauth-client-secret" in the list, and paste in the two values taken from the Google Cloud console. The secret only shows with the "Show sensitive data" button. The token, the account and the listing fill themselves in at the next step.
On the page you want, add a "Collection" block and pick the "Customer reviews" source. Reviews are shown with their rating, their date and the link to the original review.

This first part happens at Google and takes 7 to 10 business days: access to the Business Profile API, then publishing the OAuth app. The help procedure "Display your listing's Google reviews" gives the links and the exact order. Come back here once access is granted.

The arrow button opens the public reply, which goes to Google as soon as it is saved. The text and the rating of a review belong to its author: neither can be edited nor deleted. An abusive review is reported to Google.
Every review the site holds, whatever the platform. Google's come in on their own every night: the list stays empty until the first synchronization has run.

The reviews come in on their own every night, the "c975l:social:reviews:sync" task being scheduled by the bundle itself. One optional key is left, "social-google-listing-url": the public address of the listing, carried into the site's structured data.
Click "Connect" on the "LinkedIn" tile, then grant access with the profile's LinkedIn account. The site stores the token and the profile by itself.

Search for "social-linkedin-client-id" and "social-linkedin-client-secret" in the list, and paste in the app's two values. The secret only shows with the "Show sensitive data" button. The token and the profile fill themselves in at the next step.

This part happens on linkedin.com/developers: create an app attached to a LinkedIn Page you administer, add it the "Share on LinkedIn" and "Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect" products, and declare the site's address followed by "/social/linkedin/callback" as its redirect URL. Come back here with the app's ID and secret.
Unchecked, the name is still read by screen readers: it leaves the screen, never the accessibility.
Create it if it does not exist yet, open it otherwise: there is only one for the whole site.
One row per network: its icon, the address of your page over there, and a label if you want to replace the network's own.
Plain icon, badge in the network's own colors, a ring filling in on hover, or text only with no icon. The preview right below shows the result.
Optional: a line above the icons, inviting visitors to follow you. Left empty, nothing at all is rendered.
Your networks are not page content: they are entered once here, and the site picks them up everywhere.
Add the social links block to a page or to the footer: it renders this list, wherever it sits.
Click "Connect" on the "Facebook & Instagram" tile, then grant access with the Facebook account managing the Page. The site stores the Page, its token and the Instagram account by itself.

Search for "social-meta-app-id" and "social-meta-app-secret" in the list, and paste in the app's two values. The secret only shows with the "Show sensitive data" button. For an account managing several Pages, fill in "social-meta-page-id" too, or the first one is taken. The token and the Instagram account fill themselves in at the next step.

This part happens on developers.facebook.com: create an app, add Facebook Login to it with the site's address followed by "/social/meta/callback" as redirect URI, and leave it in development mode. The Page must be linked to the Instagram professional account. Come back here with the app's ID and secret.
This button approves the post: it goes out on its own at its planned date, instead of being sent at once. Tick several drafts to approve them together with "Approve the selection".
For a post prepared from the site, "Change the content" takes another photo: drawn again in the same gallery, or chosen among those still free. Its texts are written again for it.
The edit button opens the post: one text per network, each limited to the length that network accepts, under the photos or the video going out with it.
Every post has its date and time. Those in draft wait here for your reading, then your approval.
"From an address" prepares a draft of any page, of this site or another one, from its Open Graph tags, at the date chosen.
Back on the list, the paper-plane button sends the post to every network that has not taken it yet. A network refusing keeps its error message, and "Publish" tries it again.
Prepares several drafts at once, every day, week or month: one text, texts written by the AI from an instruction, or the site's next contents. They are then read and approved, one by one or together.
A draft every N days (1 every day, 2 every other day, 7 every week), on some days of the week or every month, from the moment chosen.
The drafts are created and the calendar opens on the first one: proofread them, then approve them one by one or together.
One text for all, texts written by the AI from an instruction, or the site's next contents, each with its own text.
The series screen, which "Generate a series" also opens from the posts and the calendar: how many drafts, from when, on which networks.
An email warns when the series comes near its end. "Prolong the series", on the screen of one of its posts, makes as many again after it, at the same pace.
Optional: a short id ("share") so a menu entry can point straight at the band. Without an anchor, it is still reached by scrolling the page.
Open any published page: the buttons are there, with the look you have just given them. Hovering the band raises a button bringing you straight back here.
The "share this page" line above the buttons: its wording is the site's own, only its display is set here.
Create them if they do not exist yet, open them otherwise: there is only one set for the whole site.
The preview right below updates on every change, before anything is even saved.
Tick the ones you want, and drag them: the order of the list is the order shown.
The share buttons show on your pages: what is set here is which ones, and what they look like. If a warning says they are disabled, turn them back on first.
Wide, square or round button: that is the room the buttons take under your pages.

Copy this address into your calendar: Evolution, New then "On the web" calendar; Google Calendar, Other calendars then "From URL" (then shown on Android); Outlook, Add calendar then "Subscribe from web". Read-only, refreshed by the calendar at its own pace. Keep it secret: renewing it cuts the former one.
Create a secret address to see the posts in your calendar, read-only.
A gallery file: it is changed in the gallery, and never deleted with the post.

In the order they go out. A photo is stored as a JPEG, the one format every network takes. When the site has a gallery, "Add from the site" takes a photo or a video from it. With no photo nor video, a post prepared from a content goes out with that content's picture. Each ticked network's rules are checked when saving, and the approval is refused while a network does not take the medias.
The date and time the post goes out once approved, to the quarter of an hour.
Untick a network not to post there; tick one to get a text written for it, shown the next time the post is opened. A greyed network is not connected: see "Connections".
The post's text, rephrased or translated with Donovan. Each network gets a copy cut to its length, editable afterwards network by network; changing this text writes them all again.
In days, for "Every N days": 1 every day, 2 every other day, 7 every week.
Optional: attached to every post written here, stored once, instead of the pictures of the contents ticked.
With the site's contents, nothing ticked takes them all, in turn. With a text or the AI, each post takes a picture at random among the ones ticked, reserved for it and changeable on its screen.
Each post's text or, with the AI, what they are about: the AI writes a different take for each, at the length of the shortest network ticked. Not needed for the site's contents.
Short id to link a menu entry to this band (e.g. "share"). Without an anchor, it can't be targeted from a menu.

The share buttons are turned off for the whole site: no page shows them, so these settings have no effect for now.
Default networks/style for share buttons - a singleton, overridable per page via the "share_buttons_display" block. Edit the active networks, their order and the display style.
The posts calendar: what went out, and every coming post at its date and time. Click a post to open it.

The networks the site connects to. Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and Bluesky receive the posts prepared on the "Posts" screen: publishing starts as soon as one of them is connected, nothing else to turn on. Google gives access to the reviews of your Business Profile.
"%title%": draw another content at random in the same group, or choose one among those neither reserved nor published. The former one is freed.
Site-wide social links shown in the footer - a singleton, one set of links. Edit the list to add, remove or reorder a social network.

Tick the site's photos or videos to add to "%title%", after its medias. A photo is copied as a JPEG for the post, a video stays the site's own. Save the post first: its unsaved changes are not carried over.
The address of a page, of this site or another one: its title, summary and sharing image become a post, to review before publishing.

The posts prepared for your networks, one text per network, each at its date. Those in draft wait for your reading: correct the texts, save, then click "Approve" for it to go out at its date, or "Publish" to send it at once. Deleting a post cancels it.

Prepares a series of drafts at once, at a steady pace. They show in red on the calendar: read them, correct them, then approve them one by one or together from the list. Once the series has gone out, generate a new one.
"%title%": %count% more draft(s), with the same settings, after the last post of %date%.
